result.title: Assembly-JEPA: Using World Models for Fine-Grained Industrial Image Verification
result.summary: Automated verification of industrial assembly processes remains a challenging problem due to substantial visual variability, limited availability of labeled defect data, and the fine-grained nature of many assembly errors. Existing approaches often rely on object detection, CAD models, or supervised classification pipelines, which can struggle to generalize across changing products and assembly configurations. In this work, we propose a novel self-supervised assembly verification framework based on Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs). Starting from the JEPA-based world model LeWorldModel, we investigate how the architecture must be adapted to verify the correctness of fine-grained assembly operations. To this end, we formulate assembly verification as a predictive world modeling task operating on before-and-after observations of assembly processes. Experimental results on industrial assembly tasks demonstrate that the proposed approach reliably detects both fine-grained incorrect assembly states and action-state mismatches, achieving an AUROC of 86.9% on a newly introduced assembly verification dataset. These results indicate that JEPA-based predictive representations constitute a promising foundation for robust and data-efficient industrial assembly verification.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将工业装配正确性验证重构为预测式世界建模任务，基于 JEPA 世界模型 LeWorldModel，用装配前后的观测做自监督预测表示，以检测细粒度错误状态与动作-状态不匹配，并在新数据集上报告 AUROC 86.9%。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「前后观测预测 + 预测表示判别状态是否一致」的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态是否保留任务必要视觉细节、以及如何用预测误差作为证据/验证信号提供可核查线索，但属非语言模型场景，迁移需较多确认。
